Comprehensive Research on "Killer Websites" and Reusable Frameworks 2025:

KILLER WEBSITE PATTERNS 2025:
1. Performance-First UX: Fast, efficient websites with intentional motion design
2. AI-Driven Personalization: Real-time content adaptation based on user behavior
3. Interactive Elements: Micro-animations, hover effects, scroll-triggered animations
4. Bold Visual Language: Dopamine colors (neon pinks, electric blues), nature-inspired organic shapes
5. Experimental Navigation: Radial menus, gesture-based navigation, custom cursors
6. AR/VR Integration: Virtual try-ons, immersive shopping experiences
7. Sustainability Focus: Energy-efficient design, reduced carbon footprint
8. Emotionally Intelligent Design: Empathetic error messages, mood-adaptive interfaces

SUCCESSFUL REUSABLE FRAMEWORK PATTERNS:
1. Leading Libraries: MUI (comprehensive), Ant Design (enterprise-grade), Chakra UI (accessibility-first), Next UI (modern/fast)

1. Over-fragmentation: Creating too many micro-components causing codebase sprawl
2. Style Scattered: Definitions spread across units, causing repetition and inconsistency
3. Over-customization: Leading to inconsistent UI during library updates
4. Organizational Barriers: Lack of proper feedback loops, economic investment challenges
5. Premature Complexity: Adding features before simple base is established

DUAL-PURPOSE BEST PRACTICES:
1. Start Simple: Build basic components first, add complexity only when needed
2. Clear Architecture: Well-maintained style guides, proper review processes (2+ reviewers)
3. Testing Integration: Built-in testing from start (Laravel/PHPUnit approach)
4. AI Integration: Use frameworks with AI-powered helpers for optimization
5. DevOps Mindset: Engineering for resilience, not just speed - detect, decide, recover systematically

SPEED VS QUALITY BALANCE:
- Django Approach: DRY principle maintains quality while boosting speed
- Framework Structure: Provides development speed without sacrificing maintainability
- Testing-First: Integrated testing ensures bug-free rapid development
- AI Assistance: Real-time code optimization and best practice recommendations

- GSAP sets initial states (opacity: 0, y: 50, blur) on '.hero-tagline'

- Both systems fight for control of the same properties

- GSAP: tagline animates at '-=0.5' timing (around 1s after artist name)
- Framer Motion: tagline has delay: TIMING.BEAT (0.5s)

- createHeroAnimations() called in useEffect (line 66) 
- Framer Motion animations start when isLoaded becomes true (line 244)
- Both trigger around same time, causing double-animation

ROOT CAUSE: Two animation libraries controlling same DOM elements simultaneously.
